Card:
card:question: Does widening a graph ingredient-substitution ranker raise its Hit@1 on Recipe1MSubs, once the 20.56 vs 34.53 baseline gap between two GISMo protocols is explained?
card:hypothesis: Hit@1 saturates by width 300 because GISMo already ranks 6,653 ingredients with a small GNN; more width won't help [s1].
card:sequential_part: The width sweep waits on reconciliation: reproduce Meta 20.56, then Rita 34.53, then sweep — three ordered steps.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: Hit@1 climbs with width, at least +1 point from 300 to 512, showing ranker capacity is the lever.
card:if_not: Hit@1 is flat from 300 to 512 (within seed noise), so added width does not improve substitution ranking.
card:test_summary: Run Meta's official GISMo and Rita et al.'s protocol in one harness to reproduce 20.56 and 34.53, isolate the difference; then sweep width 64-512 at 5 seeds under the reproducing protocol and report both.
card:closest_prior: Meta's GISMo paper tuned width over 200-600 and kept 300, the largest width on this axis, but reported no width trend [s1].
card:left_open: No published result reports how Hit@1 changes with ranker width 64-512 on Recipe1MSubs, under either protocol.
card:anchor: Reproduce Meta's Hit@1 20.56±0.14 [s1] with official code and data; independent 20.4 [s11].
card:limits: Shows general substitution Hit@1, not sustainability-specific substitutes; Recipe1MSubs is unlabeled for sustainability, so 'sustainable replacements' is only indirectly tested.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
reshape: Does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on, rather than run independent work side by side? 5 = restructuring names the dependency, why it need not run in order and how the plan computes it at the same time; condition says what must hold for that to pay off; condition_phase measures it before the main spend; and the closest prior does not already do this for this system; 3 = it removes a dependency, but condition is missing or is not measured before the main spend; 2 = it parallelises only within each step (splitting a large state across GPUs) or regroups and rebalances independent work (batching unfinished runs, load balancing, lower precision), leaving the chain in order; 1 = independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism, or the plan rebuilds a parallel version the closest prior already reports for this system. Reusing a method published for a different system does not lower this score.
baseline: Is the gain timed against the strongest ways to get the same answer without the plan's method? Check four conditions: (a) baseline_sequential is tuned (compiled, vectorised or multithreaded code, or a published optimised code), not a plain interpreted loop; (b) baseline_copies is timed on the same GPUs; (c) anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; (d) a named phase times every arm as time or dollars to one answer, so the gain is measured, not only modelled. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail. NA when restructuring.method is none.

Let me evaluate each criterion.

stakes: The two outcomes: if_lever (Hit@1 climbs with width ≥+1) vs if_not (flat). Does whichever occurs change a choice someone faces? This is about width capacity for substitution ranker — choosing model width for a ranker. But scope_gap: not sustainability-specific. The root question is industrial food ingredient replacement for sustainability. The test measures general substitution Hit@1, not sustainability. The choice would be "what width to use" — a modest engineering choice. Within limits in scope_gap, the outcomes bear on the root question's choice only through a step not checked (sustainability labeling). So3 seems right: outcomes bear on choice only through a step test does not check (single model / stand-in system). Actually also "one outcome is already much more likely than the other"? Hypothesis says saturation, so if_not maybe more likely. But main: it's a stand-in system (general substitution vs sustainability). Score 3, ref card:limits or card:if_lever. Ref: card:limits.

lever: (a) predicted difference ≥1 point vs noise: noise_rule says 2x pooled std, source std 0.14 → 0.28; 1 point > noise. Holds. (b) compute_axis spans 10×: 64→512 = 8×. Fails (8× < 10×). (c) varied quantity bought with compute — width is compute, yes; restructuring.method is "none", so arms condition N/A. (d) held_fixed includes splits, candidate set, etc. But protocol is being chosen — the sweep runs under both protocols; the decision rule compares 512 vs 300 presumably within the phase-A protocol. Hmm, one input that could explain: protocol differs but comparison within protocol. Seems held_fixed lists many. So one condition fails (b): 8× < 10×. Score: 3 (one fails). Actually could also argue (a) fine. So 3.

Wait — is the span 8× or does it need10×? 512/64 = 8. Fails. So value 3, ref plan:compute_axis.levels (no card line carries levels? card:method is "none"; card:question... The card doesn't state the width range64–512? card:test_summary says "sweep width 64-512". That carries the range but not explicitly the ratio. I'd use plan:compute_axis.levels. Hmm, ref should be card line that decides it, or plan field path when no card line carries it. The card:test_summary carries "width 64-512" — computing ratio 8. I'll use card:test_summary. Reason: "64–512 spans 8×, below required 10×; other three conditions hold."

verifiable: Measured outcome scored against published numbers: reproduction of20.56 within ±0.5 before trusting trend; but the actual decision outcome (if_lever vs if_not) is measured Hit@1 at widths — that's model's own output, no independent truth. However criterion: "5 = ... exact or planted truth ... and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance". The setup does reproduce published 20.56 within ±0.5 (anchor, checks). But the decision quantity (width trend) is scored against... the published choice of 300? The trend itself has no independent truth. Hmm. The criterion asks "What is the measured outcome scored against?" The measured decision outcome is Hit@1 difference — self-produced. But anchor reproduction gives an independent published number check. Is that enough for 5? The 5 requires an exact/planted truth not from method under test, plus reproduction step. Hit@1 on held-out test set is a form of ground truth labels (substitution pairs) independent of method? Recipe1MSubs test labels come from dataset, not from the method. So measured Hit@1 is scored against dataset ground truth plus the anchor reproduces published 20.56 ±0.5. That fits 5? The "exact truth" — held-out test labels are ground truth (dataset), independent of method. And reproduction step stated in anchor/checks. I'd say 5.

Hmm, but careful: could be 4 but schema only1-5. The reproduction is explicit with tolerance ±0.5. I'll give 5, ref card:anchor.

open: closest prior: Meta tuned width 200–600 kept 300, no width trend reported; left_open states no published result on 64–512. The quoted prior stops short of this range (doesn't report trend) and the plan states the gap. Score 5, ref card:left_open.

reshape: restructuring.method = "none". Criterion: does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency... method is none, sequential yes. So 1? Score 1: "independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism". Here there's no restructuring at all — the plan explicitly keeps the chain in order ("sequential: yes"). So the plan does not remove dependency. Score 1, ref card:sequential_part (or card:method "none"). Use card:method. Reason: "method is none; plan keeps reconciliation before sweep explicitly sequential, removing no dependency."

baseline: NA when restructuring.method is none. card:method = "none" → NA, ref card:method.

decides_by: earliest phase after which decision_rule can be applied whichever outcome occurs, excluding phases that only reproduce a published number or only measure throughput. Phase A reproduces Meta 20.56 (reproduction — excluded). Phase B reproduces Rita 34.53 + isolates gap (reproduction-ish, but the gate fail path: proceed with Meta protocol only — still reproduction).
